title: Finite generation conjecture for verbal subgroups
statement:
Let $w=w(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ be a group word and let $G$ be a profinite group. Write $G_w$ for the set of $w$-values in $G$, and let $w(G)$ denote the closed subgroup generated by those values.

**Finite generation conjecture.** If

$$
|G_w|<2^{\aleph_0},
$$

then $w(G)$ is generated by finitely many $w$-values.

This is presented as a weaker version of the strong conciseness conjecture. The paper does not establish it in general, although it follows in cases where strong conciseness is known together with the relevant finite-generation argument.
source_name: Eloisa Detomi, Benjamin Klopsch and Pavel Shumyatsky, “Strong conciseness in profinite groups”, arXiv:1907.01344 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.01344

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).
